{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Identity" },
  "read": "This student put in real effort and still got a bad result, which is the hardest kind of failure to metabolize. They are not slacking off — they are starting to build a story about themselves: I am just not a math person, or a science person, or whatever this subject is. That story is a self-protective move, because if the cause is fixed ability, the effort was not wasted — it was doomed. The respect angle is this: they need you to see that they tried, and they need you to refuse to confirm the story they are telling themselves.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Say something like 'This is a hard test, lots of people struggled' — which feels kind but quietly agrees that maybe they really can't do it, and lets them off the hook from trying again." },
  "mentorMove": "Validate the frustration fully, then redirect the explanation from fixed ability to specific, learnable skill — this is not who you are, this is what you have not cracked yet. Hold the expectation that they will try again with a different approach.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard stays — the work needs to be redone or the skill needs to be practiced until it lands.",
    "Do not let the fixed-ability story go unchallenged; that is the one thing you cannot quietly agree with."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them choose when and how to revisit the material — office hours, a study group, a one-on-one walkthrough with you.",
    "If a different format or problem set would reveal what broke down, use it."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I saw your score and I also know you put time into this — that gap is genuinely frustrating, and I get it." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I ask — when you were studying, which parts felt shaky and which parts felt solid? I want to understand where things broke down, not just that they did." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I think happened: the effort was real, but the strategy did not match what the material needed yet. That is a solvable problem — it is not a you problem. Let us figure out which specific piece to attack first and how you want to go after it." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am not going to let you close the door on this subject based on one result, because my standard for you is higher than that and I genuinely believe you can get there. Struggling right now means your brain is working on something hard — that is exactly where learning actually happens. Tell me one thing you are willing to try differently before the next assessment." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time this student produces any correct reasoning or improvement, name it specifically and out loud — not generic praise, but 'that move you just made, connecting those two ideas, that is exactly the thinking this subject requires.' Over weeks, you are replacing their fixed story with an evidence-based one: I am someone who figures hard things out."
}
situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.
